item.title: U.S. Strikes Iran Again, as Trump Encounters a More Determined Adversary in Widened War
item.description: The United States is again exchanging strikes with Iran, just days after the president appeared to reject plans to escalate.
item.dc:creator: Julian E. Barnes, Helene Cooper and Eric Schmitt
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: President Trump in Oakland County Michigan on Monday. The war that President Trump has been trying to bring to a diplomatic conclusion since April is now threatening to grow bigger.

item.title: U.S.-Saudi Attack on Iraqi Militias Risks Drawing Them into War
item.description: Iran-aligned militias in Iraq were under growing pressure to disarm, but the latest strikes may embolden them to get more deeply involved in the war.
item.dc:creator: Erika Solomon and Falih Hassan
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Mourners carried a coffin draped in the Iranian flag during a funeral for those killed in airstrikes on bases belonging to Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces, in Mosul on Wednesday

item.title: Families Face Anxiety, Angst as Loved Ones Are Deployed to Fight Iran
item.description: As the war with Iran has continued, some are finding that the stress is bringing back old anxieties.
item.dc:creator: Bernard Mokam and Georgia Gee
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Mental health counselors say they are attending to more military families who are reporting stress and anxiety about a conflict that has taken the lives of at least 18 service members and wounded more than 400.

item.title: How the War With Iran Is Widening, and U.S. Hospitals See a Surge of Uninsured Patients
item.description: Plus, the horrendous smell plaguing one Canadian town.

item.title: Warsh’s Performance Falls Flat With Markets as Fed Holds Rates Steady
item.description: Kevin M. Warsh has made taming inflation the top priority of his tenure as Federal Reserve chairman. But his hesitancy to embrace the possibility of higher borrowing costs has sparked a backlash.
item.dc:creator: Colby Smith
item.media:description: Traders on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange as a screen broadcasts a news conference by Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh on Wednesday.

item.title: After Obamacare Cuts, Hospitals Are Treating More Uninsured Patients
item.description: More people who lost coverage after congressional Republicans ended enhanced federal subsidies are now seeking care in emergency rooms and unable to pay bills.
item.dc:creator: Reed Abelson
item.category: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (2010)
item.media:description: Major hospitals have expressed growing concerns about the significant decrease in paying patients.

item.title: Senators Cornyn and Tillis Force Delay of Blanche Nomination Over Trump’s IRS Deal
item.description: John Cornyn and Thom Tillis accused the nominee for attorney general of refusing to put on paper his promise to kill aspects of the deal he cut to settle President Trump’s suit against the agency.
item.dc:creator: Glenn Thrush and Michael Gold
item.media:description: Todd Blanche, the acting attorney general, cannot afford to lose a single Republican vote.

item.title: Bipartisan Anger Grows at Pentagon’s Delayed ‘Forever Chemicals’ Cleanups
item.description: Hundreds of bases are contaminated with PFAS, which are linked to low birth weight and other risks. Politicians from both parties are demanding explanations.
item.dc:creator: Hiroko Tabuchi
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Nina Riggio for The New York Times
item.media:description: A burned airplane fuselage used in firefighting exercises at Cannon Air Force Base in New Mexico, a PFAS-contaminated site.

item.title: Poland’s Leader Says Russian Missile May Have Struck Its Territory During Ukraine Attack
item.description: Russian missiles have briefly entered Polish airspace in the past. Investigators have yet to definitively identify the object that struck Poland overnight.
item.dc:creator: Lara Jakes and Constant Méheut
item.media:credit: Fot. Jakub Orzechowski/Agencja Wyborcza.Pl, via Reuters
item.media:description: Emergency services at the site where an object landed near Lublin, Poland.

item.title: Russia Strikes Ukraine With Missiles and Drones, Killing at Least 8
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine said that a family of five had been killed at home in the latest in a series of large-scale aerial assaults by Moscow.
item.dc:creator: Constant Méheut
item.media:description: In Lviv, western Ukraine, on Thursday morning, at the site of a Russian missile strike. The overnight attack pushed Russia’s use of ballistic missiles to a new monthly record.

item.title: As China’s A.I. Gets Stronger, It Poses New Risks to Beijing
item.description: China’s A.I. rise is creating a new dilemma for Beijing. The open models that win influence abroad may pose risks to the country’s security and geopolitical strategy.
item.dc:creator: David Pierson and Berry Wang
item.category: Beijing Moonshot AI Technology Co Ltd
item.media:credit: Pool photo by Ng Han Guan
item.media:description: The Chinese leader Xi Jinping opening the World A.I. Conference in Shanghai, China, in July. Even as China supports openness in A.I., it needs to “constantly refine measures to forestall loss of control,” he said.

item.title: A.I. Data Centers in Space? A System to Cool Chips Could Help.
item.description: Researchers at Caltech and Sophia Space, a start-up, have developed a technology using solar power to prevent computer equipment from overheating in orbit.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Penn
item.media:description: Small solar arrays, like those on the International Space Station, are already used in space, but A.I. data centers would require substantially more equipment for electricity generation.

item.title: China Threatens Retaliation as U.S. Moves to Block Robot Imports
item.description: The dispute highlights how robotics has become the latest battleground in the intensifying technological and industrial rivalry between Washington and Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Steve Lohr and Xinyun Wu
item.media:credit: Qilai Shen for The New York Times
item.media:description: Humanoid robots on display at a convention in Shanghai last year.

item.title: Wildfires in Greece Kill 3 Firefighters as Blazes Still Burn in France and Spain
item.description: Greece also worked to contain blazes on Lesbos and in the Peloponnese, where another firefighter died, in the midst of a brutal wildfire season for Europe.
item.dc:creator: Niki Kitsantonis
item.media:description: Wildfires on the island of Crete in Greece on Wednesday.

item.title: As Wildfires Plague Europe, Scotland Races to Save a Cherished National Park
item.description: As Europe’s climate warms, even moorlands and forests in the Cairngorms, in the Scottish Highlands, have fallen victim to rapidly spreading flames.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Castle
item.media:description: Land charred by the Cairngorm wildfire, in Aviemore, Scotland, on Tuesday.

item.title: European Wildfires Amplified by Emptying Countryside and Fewer Farms
item.description: A warming planet and a shift away from farming have set the stage for larger fires on the continent. “We must learn to coexist with them,” one report said.
item.dc:creator: Raymond Zhong
item.media:description: Wildfire smoke from a fire burning west of Bordeaux, France, on Tuesday. The giant blazes in France and Spain are their largest on record.

item.title: Rescue Boat Crews Show Signs of Brain Injuries, but Coast Guard Isn’t Looking
item.description: Untreated and undiagnosed, the crews that save lives in the roughest seas face the relentless pounding of waves.
item.dc:creator: Dave Philipps

item.title: How Climate Change and Tariffs Help China Raise More Cattle
item.description: As increased rain makes grasslands and cornfields possible in areas that once were deserts, the world’s largest beef importer is becoming more self-reliant by expanding domestic herds.
item.dc:creator: Keith Bradsher
item.media:credit: Gilles Sabrié for The New York Times
item.media:description: A herder taking her cows to graze in mountain pastures in northern China’s Hebei Province.

item.title: Tossed Tuna and Furloughed Workers: Midtown’s ‘Frozen Zone’ Scrapes By
item.description: For nearly three weeks, restaurants and other small businesses in the shadow of the former Pfizer building were shut when the tower began to buckle.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Maslin Nir
item.media:credit: Angelina Katsanis for The New York Times
item.media:description: Restaurants, a hotel and many small businesses dot the stretch of 43rd Street that had remained closed for nearly three weeks after the former Pfizer building became dangerously unstable. Izakaya Futago had to toss fresh fish and furlough workers.

item.title: Work Halted at Another Office Conversion in Midtown Manhattan
item.description: The Department of Buildings ordered work to stop on certain floors at 750 Third Avenue. It’s the third conversion project to have work halted since one became dangerously unstable earlier this month.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Zaveri, Arfa Momin and Miles G. Cohen
item.media:description: 750 Third Avenue in Midtown Manhattan. Inspectors from the Department of Buildings stopped work at the building, which is being converted into apartments.

item.title: Sales Are So Low, California Wineries Are Burning Their Vineyards
item.description: The rise and fall of pinot noir symbolizes the larger struggles of the wine industry as younger generations turn to other beverages.
item.dc:creator: Soumya Karlamangla
item.media:credit: Nic Coury for The New York Times
item.media:description: Monterey County, about 100 miles south of San Francisco, is an agricultural hub that vacillates between fog-shrouded cool and a sunny maritime climate, which also makes the terrain ideal for delicate wine grapes.
